title: Oracle Backward Run
statement: Let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, let $f\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})$ be a work-tape content function, and let $p\in\mathbb{Z}$. Choose a side $s\in\mathrm{Bool}$ and a verdict $v\in\mathrm{Bool}$, and assume $p$ lies on side $s$ of the origin: if $s$ is true then $0\le p$, and if $s$ is false then $p\le 0$. For any input-head position $ip$ and output string $out$, after every integer number $u$ of steps with $u\le |p|-1$, the machine started in the backward-dispatch configuration at work-tape position $p$ has the same configuration as the one with unchanged input head and output, the same backward-dispatch state, and work-tape position $\epsilon_s(1+u)$, where $\epsilon_s=1$ if $s$ is true and $\epsilon_s=-1$ if $s$ is false.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ lies on the side of zero specified by $s$
Input-head position $ip$ is among the valid positions for $x$
